caption_used: Mean absolute values of hidden states across model layers, comparing pre-gating, post-gating, and baseline configurations. The hidden state mean before gate (blue dashed line, avg 0.71) remains near zero through approximately layer 15, then rises sharply to a peak of roughly 2.8 at layer 23. The post-gating hidden state mean (orange dotted, avg 0.05) and baseline mean (green solid, avg 0.04) both remain close to zero throughout, with the baseline showing marginally higher values than the post-gating mean in the final layers. The dramatic pre-gating increase beginning at layer 12 demonstrates that gating effectively suppresses the activation amplification observed in deeper layers.

raw_responses.Bulgarian: DESCRIPTION: The figure is a line graph titled "Hidden State Mean," illustrating the mean absolute values of hidden states across model layers for three configurations: pre-gating, post-gating, and baseline. The x-axis represents the layer number, ranging from 0 to 25 with tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis represents the absolute mean, ranging from 0 to 4 with tick marks at intervals of 1. The blue dashed line, labeled "hidden state mean before gate, avg 0.71," starts at a value of approximately 0.1 at layer 0, fluctuates slightly between 0.2 and 0.3 from layer 0 to layer 15, and then rises sharply, reaching a peak of approximately 2.8 at layer 23. The orange dotted line, labeled "hidden state mean after gate, avg 0.05," remains close to 0 across all layers, with values fluctuating between 0 and 0.05. The green solid line, labeled "hidden state mean of baseline, avg 0.04," also remains near 0, with values fluctuating between 0 and 0.05, showing slightly higher values than the post-gating mean in the final layers.
